questions.question: Give the pathway of visual impulses from the retina to the visual cortex.
questions.solution_html:

  • Lateral Geniculate Body (Thalamus) → Optic Radiations → Visual Cortex (Occipital Lobe). (NB: A clear, precise
  • flowchart showing the sequence is sufficient for full marks; no diagram or detailed explanation is needed.)

questions.question: Describe the function of the middle ear. / Mention the ordered sequence of auditory relay stations from periphery
questions.solution_html:
• ● Transmission of sound: Transfers sound vibrations from the tympanic membrane (eardrum) to the inner ear
  • through the ossicles — malleus, incus, and stapes.
  • ● Amplification: The ossicles amplify the sound vibrations to overcome the resistance of the fluid in the inner ear.
  • ● Pressure equalization: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx and helps equalize air
  • pressure on both sides of the eardrum.
  • ● Protection: The tensor tympani and stapedius muscles protect the inner ear from loud sounds by dampening
  • excessive vibrations. (Any 2 points: (1 mark) each)

questions.question: / reproductive techniques apply in her management? Mention two common physical symptoms of premenstrual dysphoric
questions.solution_html:
• A woman with PCOD complains of infertility. How do assisted reproductive techniques apply in her
  • management?
  • ● Ovulation induction therapy – Use of drugs like Clomiphene citrate, Letrozole, or Gonadotropins to stimulate
  • ovulation.
  • ● Intrauterine insemination (IUI) – Washed sperm are directly introduced into the uterus near the time of ovulation.
  • ● In vitro fertilization (IVF) – Eggs are collected, fertilized in the lab, and the resulting embryos are transferred to
  • the uterus.
  • ● Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) – A single sperm is injected directly into an egg; used when sperm count
  • or motility is low.
  • ● Laparoscopic ovarian drilling (LOD) – A surgical technique to destroy androgen-producing tissue, improving
  • ovulation.
  • ● Cryopreservation of embryos or oocytes – Useful for preserving fertility if repeated cycles are needed.
  • ● Lifestyle modification support – Though not ART itself, weight reduction and insulin-sensitizing drugs like
  • metformin enhance ART success. (Any two methods with explanations or four methods mentioned briefly can be
  • given full marks.)

questions.question: Write short notes on Graves’ disease.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Graves’ disease is an autoimmune disorder causing hyperthyroidism.
  • ● The body produces TSH receptor antibodies that overstimulate the thyroid gland.
  • ● Leads to excess secretion of thyroid hormones (T₃ and T₄).
  • ● Symptoms: weight loss, heat intolerance, rapid heartbeat, tremors, anxiety, and exophthalmos (bulging eyes).
  • ● Treatment: antithyroid drugs, radioactive iodine therapy, or partial thyroidectomy. (Liberal valuation)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Name one mood stabilizer used in the treatment of bipolar disorder.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Lithium – the most common and effective traditional mood stabilizer
  • ● Valproate (Valproic acid) – controls manic episodes
  • ● Carbamazepine – used when lithium is not tolerated
  • ● Lamotrigine – effective for preventing depressive episodes
  • ● Atypical antipsychotics – such as olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone for mood stabilization
  • ● Psychotherapy – cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) helps manage mood swings
  • ● Mindfulness and meditation – reduce stress and emotional instability
  • ● Regular sleep schedule – stabilizes mood and prevents manic/depressive triggers
  • ● Physical exercise – boosts endorphins and supports emotional balance
  • ● Avoidance of alcohol and recreational drugs – prevents worsening of symptoms
  • ● Support groups and family therapy – improve emotional regulation and adherence to treatment. (Any one
  • stabilizer - (2 mark) or a general description can give full marks- Liberal valuation)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how nociceptors are involved in the perception of pain through / the skin.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Nociceptors are specialized sensory receptors in the skin that detect painful or damaging stimuli such as extreme
  • heat, pressure, or chemicals.
  • ● When activated, they generate nerve impulses that travel through sensory neurons to the spinal cord.
  • ● These impulses are then relayed to the brain, particularly the thalamus and somatosensory cortex, where pain is
  • perceived.
  • ● This mechanism helps the body recognize and respond to potential harm, promoting protective actions like
  • withdrawal from the source of injury. (definition:(1 mark), Comment: (3 marks) or a good account on nociceptors: 4
  • marks)

questions.question: Describe the important functions of endocrine system in our body.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Regulates metabolism: Controls energy production and nutrient use through hormones like insulin and thyroxine.
  • ● Maintains homeostasis: Keeps internal conditions stable, including blood pressure, temperature, and water
  • balance.
  • ● Controls growth and development: Growth hormone and thyroid hormones promote body growth and tissue
  • development.
  • ● Regulates reproduction: Hormones like estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone control sexual development and
  • fertility.
  • ● Coordinates stress response: Adrenal hormones such as cortisol and adrenaline help the body respond to stress.
  • ● Regulates mood and behavior: Hormones influence emotions, sleep, and mental well-being.
  • ● Regulates blood glucose levels: Insulin and glucagon maintain normal blood sugar balance.
  • ● Controls calcium and bone metabolism: Parathyroid hormone and calcitonin regulate calcium levels and bone
  • strength.
  • ● Influences circadian rhythm: Melatonin from the pineal gland controls sleep–wake cycles.
  • ● Aids in digestion: Hormones like gastrin, secretin, and cholecystokinin regulate digestive processes.
  • ● Supports immune function: Thymosin promotes immune cell development.
  • ● Regulates blood pressure and fluid balance: Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone (ADH) maintain water and salt
  • balance.
  • ● Promotes cell repair and regeneration: Growth factors assist in tissue maintenance and healing.
  • ● Integrates with the nervous system: Works with the hypothalamus to coordinate body responses to internal and
  • external changes. (Explain any 4 points with brief explanations – (4 marks) or mention any correct 6 points- 4
  • marks)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the interaction between sympathetic nervous system and / adrenal medulla in stress. Discuss how hormonal changes in the ovaries prepare the female body
questions.solution_html:
• ● During stress, the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is activated as part of the “fight or flight” response.
  • ● The SNS stimulates the adrenal medulla (inner part of the adrenal gland) through sympathetic nerve fibers.
  • ● The adrenal medulla then releases epinephrine (adrenaline) and norepinephrine (noradrenaline) into the
  • bloodstream.
  • ● These hormones increase heart rate, blood pressure, respiration, and glucose release, preparing the body to handle
  • stress.
  • ● This shows a close coordination where the SNS provides rapid nerve stimulation, and the adrenal medulla ensures
  • a prolonged hormonal effect to manage stress efficiently. (Give full marks for relevant explanation)
questions.final_answer: a prolonged hormonal effect to manage stress efficiently. (Give full marks for relevant explanation)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: / for fertilization and implantation.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Follicular phase: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) promotes the growth of ovarian follicles, which secrete
  • estrogen. Estrogen thickens the endometrium and prepares the cervix for sperm entry.
  • ● Ovulation: A surge in luteinizing hormone (LH) triggers the release of an egg (ovum) from the ovary.
  • ● Luteal phase: After ovulation, the corpus luteum forms and secretes progesterone and some estrogen.
  • ● Progesterone stabilizes and further thickens the endometrium, making it suitable for implantation.
  • ● If fertilization occurs, progesterone continues to support the uterine lining; if not, hormone levels drop, leading to
  • menstruation. ((1 mark) each for mentioning each phase (follicular, ovulation, luteal, and outcome) along with the
  • specific hormone involved and its function.)
questions.final_answer: specific hormone involved and its function.)

questions.solution_html:
• ● Because it controls and regulates the activity of other endocrine glands such as the thyroid, adrenal, and
  • reproductive glands by secreting hormones that influence their functions.(Give full marks for relevant

questions.question: Write short notes on Graves’ disease.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Graves’ disease is an autoimmune disorder causing hyperthyroidism.
  • ● The body produces TSH receptor antibodies that overstimulate the thyroid gland.
  • ● Leads to excess secretion of thyroid hormones (T₃ and T₄).
  • ● Symptoms: weight loss, heat intolerance, rapid heartbeat, tremors, anxiety, and exophthalmos (bulging eyes).
  • ● Treatment: antithyroid drugs, radioactive iodine therapy, or partial thyroidectomy. (Liberal valuation)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Name one mood stabilizer used in the treatment of bipolar disorder.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Lithium – the most common and effective traditional mood stabilizer
  • ● Valproate (Valproic acid) – controls manic episodes
  • ● Carbamazepine – used when lithium is not tolerated
  • ● Lamotrigine – effective for preventing depressive episodes
  • ● Atypical antipsychotics – such as olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone for mood stabilization
  • ● Psychotherapy – cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) helps manage mood swings
  • ● Mindfulness and meditation – reduce stress and emotional instability
  • ● Regular sleep schedule – stabilizes mood and prevents manic/depressive triggers
  • ● Physical exercise – boosts endorphins and supports emotional balance
  • ● Avoidance of alcohol and recreational drugs – prevents worsening of symptoms
  • ● Support groups and family therapy – improve emotional regulation and adherence to treatment. (Any one
  • stabilizer - (2 mark) or a general description can give full marks- Liberal valuation)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe the functional importance of olfaction in daily life activities.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Detection of hazards: Helps identify dangers such as smoke, gas leaks, or spoiled food.
  • ● Enhancement of taste: Works with taste buds to create the perception of flavor.
  • ● Emotional connection: Certain smells evoke memories and emotions.
  • ● Social communication: Body odor and perfumes influence social interactions and attraction.
  • ● Appetite regulation: Pleasant food odors stimulate appetite, while unpleasant ones suppress it.
  • ● Environmental awareness: Helps recognize surroundings and personal hygiene. (Explanation of any 4 points- 4
  • marks or a good account on functional importance - (4 marks))
questions.final_answer: marks or a good account on functional importance - )

questions.question: Explain the different primary taste sensations and give examples.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Sweet: Caused by sugars and some amino acids — e.g., candy, honey, fruits.
  • ● Sour: Produced by acids — e.g., lemon, vinegar.
  • ● Salty: Due to salts, mainly sodium ions — e.g., table salt, chips.
  • ● Bitter: Often from alkaloids — e.g., coffee, cocoa, neem.
  • ● Umami: A savory taste from glutamate and certain amino acids — e.g., meat, cheese, soy sauce.
  • (Mentioning all five primary tastes and example :(2 mark), Brief explanation:(2 marks))
questions.final_answer: (Mentioning all five primary tastes and example :, Brief explanation:)

questions.question: Explain how nociceptors are involved in the perception of pain through / the skin.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Nociceptors are specialized sensory receptors in the skin that detect painful or damaging stimuli such as extreme
  • heat, pressure, or chemicals.
  • ● When activated, they generate nerve impulses that travel through sensory neurons to the spinal cord.
  • ● These impulses are then relayed to the brain, particularly the thalamus and somatosensory cortex, where pain is
  • perceived.
  • ● This mechanism helps the body recognize and respond to potential harm, promoting protective actions like
  • withdrawal from the source of injury. (definition:(1 mark), Comment: (3 marks) or a good account on nociceptors: 4
  • marks)

questions.question: Describe the important functions of endocrine system in our body.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Regulates metabolism: Controls energy production and nutrient use through hormones like insulin and thyroxine.
  • ● Maintains homeostasis: Keeps internal conditions stable, including blood pressure, temperature, and water
  • balance.
  • ● Controls growth and development: Growth hormone and thyroid hormones promote body growth and tissue
  • development.
  • ● Regulates reproduction: Hormones like estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone control sexual development and
  • fertility.
  • ● Coordinates stress response: Adrenal hormones such as cortisol and adrenaline help the body respond to stress.
  • ● Regulates mood and behavior: Hormones influence emotions, sleep, and mental well-being.
  • ● Regulates blood glucose levels: Insulin and glucagon maintain normal blood sugar balance.
  • ● Controls calcium and bone metabolism: Parathyroid hormone and calcitonin regulate calcium levels and bone
  • strength.
  • ● Influences circadian rhythm: Melatonin from the pineal gland controls sleep–wake cycles.
  • ● Aids in digestion: Hormones like gastrin, secretin, and cholecystokinin regulate digestive processes.
  • ● Supports immune function: Thymosin promotes immune cell development.
  • ● Regulates blood pressure and fluid balance: Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone (ADH) maintain water and salt
  • balance.
  • ● Promotes cell repair and regeneration: Growth factors assist in tissue maintenance and healing.
  • ● Integrates with the nervous system: Works with the hypothalamus to coordinate body responses to internal and
  • external changes. (Explain any 4 points with brief explanations – (4 marks) or mention any correct 6 points- 4
  • marks)

questions.question: Explain the interaction between sympathetic nervous system and / adrenal medulla in stress. Discuss how hormonal changes in the ovaries prepare the female body
questions.solution_html:
• ● During stress, the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is activated as part of the “fight or flight” response.
  • ● The SNS stimulates the adrenal medulla (inner part of the adrenal gland) through sympathetic nerve fibers.
  • ● The adrenal medulla then releases epinephrine (adrenaline) and norepinephrine (noradrenaline) into the
  • bloodstream.
  • ● These hormones increase heart rate, blood pressure, respiration, and glucose release, preparing the body to handle
  • stress.
  • ● This shows a close coordination where the SNS provides rapid nerve stimulation, and the adrenal medulla ensures
  • a prolonged hormonal effect to manage stress efficiently. (Give full marks for relevant explanation)
questions.final_answer: a prolonged hormonal effect to manage stress efficiently. (Give full marks for relevant explanation)

questions.question: / for fertilization and implantation.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Follicular phase: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) promotes the growth of ovarian follicles, which secrete
  • estrogen. Estrogen thickens the endometrium and prepares the cervix for sperm entry.
  • ● Ovulation: A surge in luteinizing hormone (LH) triggers the release of an egg (ovum) from the ovary.
  • ● Luteal phase: After ovulation, the corpus luteum forms and secretes progesterone and some estrogen.
  • ● Progesterone stabilizes and further thickens the endometrium, making it suitable for implantation.
  • ● If fertilization occurs, progesterone continues to support the uterine lining; if not, hormone levels drop, leading to
  • menstruation. ((1 mark) each for mentioning each phase (follicular, ovulation, luteal, and outcome) along with the
  • specific hormone involved and its function.)
questions.final_answer: specific hormone involved and its function.)
